newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian Industry Minister Murasoli Maran says the industry sector will post higher growth in the last quarter of 1996/97 (April-March).
"I think we can attain double-digit industrial growth
and we are optimistic about growth in the last quarter. Let us wait and see," Maran told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
"The last quarter growth will be encouraging." India
expects industry to grow at 12 percent in the current financial year ending on March 31. The sector grew at 12 percent in 1995/96 against 9.4 percent the previous year.

** India's oil pool deficit is estimated to touch a high of 184 billion rupees by end of fiscal year 1996/97, according to latest estimates drawn up by the ministry of petroleum, the daily Economic Times reports.
The paper quoted officials as saying this will put
further pressure on the government to take immediate steps to cut the oil pool deficit.
** The government is veering round to the view that pension and provident funds should not invest in capital market instruments, the Business Standard reports.
Instead, the funds should divert a part of the corpus to
debt and equity schemes of financial institutions especially, the Unit Trust of India, the paper says.
** Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) taps the private placement market by offering 15 percent taxable five-year bonds, the Financial Express says.
The firm plans to raise 15 billion rupees through the
private placement route, the paper says.
MARKETS:
** Indian pivotals staged a small rally towards close of trade on Thursday, boosted by a spate of speculative buy orders, traders said.
** The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index .BSESN rose 47.88 points, or 1.43 percent, to end at 3,402.60 off the intra-day high of 3,404.11.
** The Delhi index .DE gained 0.78 percent to 724.53.
** The Calcutta index .CALSN rose 0.63 percent to 439.79.
